images.title: Why circled numbers are prime
images.purpose: Show that a circled number has exactly two factors, while a crossed-out number has more.
images.composition: Two separate cards side by side with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Left card: the number 7 circled in teal #0072B2, with its factors 1 and 7 below. Right card: the number 6 crossed in grey #6B7280, with its factors 1, 2, 3 and 6 below. Exactly 2 cards, 2 factors on the left, 4 factors on the right.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any factor list that differs from 1, 7 and 1, 2, 3, 6
images.takeaway: Circled means two factors only; crossed out means more.
images.description: A card with 7 circled and factors 1 and 7, beside a card with 6 crossed out and factors 1, 2, 3, 6.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the factors on each card and say which number is prime.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
